appliesTo: Resident individuals below 60, taxable income up to ₹50 lakh (no surcharge)
source: Slabs, rebate, cess and surcharge threshold: Income Tax Department e-filing portal, 'Salaried Individuals for AY 2026-27' (incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/individual/return-applicable-1). Standard deduction (₹75,000 new, ₹50,000 old) and the new-regime rebate edge of ₹12,70,590 (marginal relief): CBDT ITR-1 validation rules AY 2026-27, rules 112, 191, 192, 215. Unchanged for tax year 2026-27: PIB New India Samachar, February 2026, p. 25 ('No changes have been made to the income tax slabs or exemptions').

capitalGains.source: PIB, 'Union Budget 2024-25: Key Tax Reforms and Relief Measures' (July 2024): long-term gains on all financial and non-financial assets 12.5% without indexation; exemption on equity gains raised to ₹1.25 lakh a year from FY 2024-25; short-term gains on specified financial assets 20%. ₹1,25,000 exemption also in CBDT ITR-1 validation rules AY 2026-27, rule 217. Unchanged for tax year 2026-27 (PIB New India Samachar, February 2026, p. 25). Holding periods (listed securities one year, all other assets two years): CBDT FAQs on the new capital-gains regime, PIB release PRID 2036604 (July 2024); units held 12 months or less are treated as short-term.

deductions.source: Income Tax Department e-filing portal, 'Salaried Individuals for AY 2026-27' (incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/individual/return-applicable-1), read 26 Oct 2026: 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1) combined ₹1,50,000; 80CCD(1B) ₹50,000; 80D ₹25,000 for self, spouse and children and ₹25,000 for parents (₹50,000 each if a senior citizen), preventive check-up ₹5,000 within these; interest on a home loan for a self-occupied house ₹2,00,000 (24(b)); 80TTA savings interest ₹10,000; 80E education-loan interest with no limit; employer's NPS contribution 80CCD(2) up to 14% of salary in the new regime, and in the old regime 10% (14% if the employer is the Central or a State Government). Only 80CCD(2) is allowed in the new regime among these. Unchanged for tax year 2026-27 (PIB New India Samachar, February 2026: no changes to slabs or exemptions); under the Income-tax Act, 2025, 80C is now section 123 and 80D section 126 (incometaxindia.gov.in section pages).

hra.source: House rent allowance exemption (old regime only): the least of HRA received, rent paid minus 10% of salary, and 50% of salary in the large cities or 40% elsewhere, salary meaning basic pay, dearness allowance that counts for retirement benefits, and commission at a fixed percentage of turnover (incometaxindia.gov.in, 'Deductions/Allowances allowed to a salaried employee'). From tax year 2026-27 the 50% cities are Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 notified by CBDT on 20 Mar 2026 (Business Standard, 25 Mar 2026); the rule text itself could not be opened to cross-check.
